title: add vpc control plane provisioning: multi-az subnets, endpoints, sgs, peering, route53
author: Samira Patel
title_summary: Provision VPC control plane networking and DNS for Private deployments (multi-AZ)
description:
Motivation:
This PR adds Terraform modules and accompanying docs to provision the VPC networking required for Redwood Private control planes in multi-AZ setups. It standardizes subnet layout, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation so operator teams can bootstrap Private control planes with automated infrastructure-as-code.

What this changes (high-level):
- New Terraform module: modules/vpc-control-plane that creates: multi-AZ private subnets, NAT/route tables for control-plane bastions, interface endpoints (SQS, S3, ECR, KMS where applicable), and security groups scoped for control-plane components.
- VPC peering configuration with automatic route table propagation and cross-account security group helpers for common enterprise setups.
- Route53 private hosted zone and delegated records for control-plane.internal.redwood.local (configurable), plus Terraform outputs for zone IDs to wire to tenant VPCs.
- Optional interface endpoints + endpoint policy templates (for customers who want tighter service access).
- Example root module in examples/private-vpc showing multi-account/multi-region usage and a small migration guide from the older single-AZ layout.
- Helm chart values note: added a values reference for privateDNS.zoneId which is now surfaced in the installer README to accept the Route53 zone created by this module.
- Acceptance tests: terraform plan unit tests and a lightweight terratest scenario to validate subnets/routes/peering when run in an ephemeral account.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module with variables, outputs, and docs
- [x] Example usage in examples/private-vpc
- [x] Helm/installer README update to surface DNS/zoneId param
- [x] CI unit tests for terraform fmt/validate and plan-only smoke
- [x] Security review: scoped SGs and least-privilege IAM for cross-account peering role

Commits (summary):
- add modules/vpc-control-plane core resources and variables (subnets, routes, RTs)
- add endpoints module and endpoint policy templates
- add peering module with cross-account-assume-role support
- add route53 module and DNS delegation outputs
- add examples/private-vpc multi-az usage and migration notes
- update private-installer README to document privateDNS.zoneId and upgrade steps
- add terratest/plan smoke test harness and CI job

Files changed (high level):
- modules/vpc-control-plane/main.tf
- modules/vpc-control-plane/variables.tf
- modules/vpc-control-plane/outputs.tf
- modules/vpc-endpoints/* (security/policy templates)
- modules/vpc-peering/* (assume role, route propagation helpers)
- modules/route53-control-plane/*
- examples/private-vpc/main.tf
- docs/private-deployments/vpc-control-plane.md (new)
- infra/ci/terraform-plan-check.yaml (new job)
- helm/private-installer/README.md (updated)

Notes on design decisions:
- Multi-AZ by default: module creates three AZ subnets when region supports it and exposes variable to override. This provides better HA for control plane services that expect distributed endpoints.
- Endpoint policies are opt-in; some regulated customers require restricted access and we expose templates and a boolean flag.
- Peering uses a cross-account assume role when peering with customer-managed VPCs this reduces manual steps in partner setups.
- DNS ownership: module creates a private hosted zone but exposes the zone ID to allow installer/helm to attach records rather than forcing the installer to own DNS.

Backward compatibility and upgrade path:
- The existing single-az module is unchanged; the new module lives alongside and is opt-in for upgrades.
- Migration guide included in examples/private-vpc/migration.md describing steps to create the new network and cut traffic over.

Testing and CI:
- New CI job runs terraform fmt, validate, and terraform plan with sample inputs.
- Added a terratest job that can be run manually against a sandbox account to assert route tables, endpoints, and peering.

Security review summary:
- Security reviewers requested narrower SG defaults; updated SG rules to restrict CIDR and limit port ranges to only the ports used by control-plane services.
- Added IAM policy with least privilege for peering role.

Release notes:
- "Added Terraform module to provision multi-AZ VPC networking, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 private DNS for Redwood Private control planes. See docs/private-deployments/vpc-control-plane.md for usage and migration guidance."

Merge outcome:
Merged via squash-merge after approvals and a green CI run.

upgrade_instructions:
See examples/private-vpc/migration.md  
 high level: 1) deploy new vpc-control-plane module in parallel, 2) create peering and update route tables, 3) update installer values with privateDNS.zoneId, 4) perform cutover and decommission legacy single-az network.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps default configs conservative. Operators should review CIDR choices and endpoint opt-ins for their compliance posture.
testing_instructions: Run infra/ci/terraform-plan-check.yaml to validate templating; for full verification run tests/terratest with an isolated sandbox account as described in docs/private-deployments/vpc-control-plane.md.
